entry.title: Tributary 1.2.4
entry.summary: Heard grooving on an MPC One, OS 3.10.1.12, with a Digitone II. Bright notes were crackling. The machine is 48 kHz and the MPC track is 44.1, and the join was a straight line, so the top of a melody folded back into the note. The track now uses a short filter. Drums had been covering it. The spare is also long enough for the MPC's 256-sample block, about 11 ms. A shorter spare ran out at the end of each chunk and repeated a sample. entry.title: Tributary 1.2.3
entry.summary: The track resamples. Overbridge machines send 48 kHz, and the MPC track is 44.1, so what you hear on the track is Tributary's conversion, kept in time with the MPC. Capture writes a different file: the machine's own 48 kHz samples for the switches that are on, for a whole number of bars. That wav is not the resampled track. Load it like any other 48 kHz sample. entry.title: Tributary 1.1.0
entry.summary: One Tributary can sum the outputs you switch on, onto the MPC track it sits on. The switches come from the connected machine. A Digitone II still shows MAIN, ACTIVE, 1–16, DLY, REV, CHO, and IN. A Digitakt, Syntakt, or the other listed machines show their own names. A fresh copy starts with Main on. An older project that saved a single source opens with only that output on, so leave Main off when you are splitting the machine across tracks. entry.title: Tributary 1.0.0
entry.summary: Digitone II is the machine this has been heard on. Other Overbridge devices are listed and untested. - One stereo pair, or one mono channel copied to both sides, on the track the plugin sits on. Copies share one USB read. - Use the MPC as the clock. Clock from the Digitone wobbles, because it shares the USB cable with the audio. - A few milliseconds of latency remains. The plugin cannot delay the other tracks. - This zip is the 32-bit ARM build.
